newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan makes offer to WTO on financial services - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan makes offer to WTO on financial services - MOF.

text.p: Japan will make an "ambitious" offer to remove restrictions on foreign financial services firms to a World Trade Organisation (WTO) committee on Friday in a bid to boost current talks on a global pact in the sector, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Friday.

"Submission of such an ambitious offer firmly demonstrates Japan's willingness to make a positive contribution to, and to work together with, all the other members toward the successful conclusion of the negotiations within the agreed time frame," he said in a statement.
The deadline for an agreement on a pact that would open up markets in developed and developing countries for banking, insurance and securities is the end of the year.

The major industrialised nations had promised to make fresh offers by July 14 to give impetus to the talks, which have been bogged down by the unwillingness of key emerging nations to open their fledgling financial service industries to global competition.

The Japanese offer contains measures which the government already announced this year, including steps accompanying revisions to Japan's insurance and foreign exchange regulations, a Finance Ministry official said.
Under the offer, foreign insurance firms will be allowed to offer services to Japanese people without opening offices in Japan, and to enter the insurance broking business.
Foreign exchange decontrol will eliminate numerous anachronistic regulations on cross-border transactions and allow corporations and individuals to deal directly with overseas banks and brokers.

"Japan strongly hopes that our initiative will be echoed by other members...and their presentation of meaningful improvements to the schedule, which would lead to the successful conclusion of the talks," Mitsuzuka said.
